newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq to rebuild border post with Syria - papers.
newsitem.headline: Iraq to rebuild border post with Syria - papers.

text.p: Iraq said on Monday that work would start next week to rebuild and expand a border post with Syria, closed since the beginning of the 1980s, to help resume trade.

Al-Thawra, the newspaper of the ruling Baath party, quoted Minister of Housing and Reconstruction Maan Abdullah Sarsam as saying "the ministry...will start next week works to develop and expand al-Tanf border point between Iraq and Syria".
Sarsam said his ministry had begun work to maintain the highway leading to the border with Syria to ease trade and travel.
An Iraqi economic team is in Damascus discussing with officials what Syria could sell to Iraq under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

The deal allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil between last December and June to raise money to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, hit by U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The U.N. Security Council last week extended the programme for six more months.
Syrian officials have said that Syria's ports in the Mediterranean are ready to handle Iraq's purchases under the deal.

Syria's relations with Baghdad deteriorated in 1980 when Damascus sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war and further worsened with Syrian troops joining the U.S.-led force that drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991.
